terms.meaning: Figures that are exact copies, with the same shape and the same size. One fits exactly on the other.
The vertices, sides and angles that match when one figure is placed on the other. The order in △ABC ≅ △XYZ shows the matching: A with X, B with Y, C with Z.
The angle between two given sides of a triangle.

items.name: When simple figures are congruent
items.formula: Circles: same radius. Squares: same side.
items.example: Rectangles need the same length and the same breadth.

items.name: SAS
items.formula: Two sides and the angle between them are equal
items.example: Sides 5 and 7 with 40° between them fix the triangle.

items.name: ASA
items.formula: Two angles and the side between them are equal
items.example: Angles 50° and 60° with a 6 cm side between them fix the triangle.

items.name: AAS
items.formula: Two angles and another side are equal
items.example: If two angles match, the third matches too, so 180° − 50° − 60° = 70° in both.

items.name: RHS
items.formula: Right angle, hypotenuse and one side are equal
items.example: Right triangles with hypotenuse 13 and side 5 are congruent. The other side is 12 in both.

items.name: AAA
items.formula: Equal angles do not fix the size
items.example: Equilateral triangles with sides 2 cm and 5 cm have the same angles but are not congruent.

items.name: SSA
items.formula: Two sides and an angle not between them are not enough
items.example: Two different triangles can fit the same SSA values.

items.name: Isosceles triangle
items.formula: Angles opposite equal sides are equal
items.example: If the top angle is 40°, each base angle is (180° − 40°) ÷ 2 = 70°.

mistakes.text: The order of letters matters. If △ABC ≅ △XYZ, then AB = XY, not AB = YZ.
Equal angles alone do not make triangles congruent. They can have different sizes.
In SAS the angle must be between the two sides. If it is not, the condition is SSA, which does not work.
